title:
Diving into the noradrenergic system : Role of the alpha2C-adrenergic receptors
NA2C-TEP-IRM
official:
Diving into the noradrenergic system : Role of the alpha2C-adrenergic receptors
NA2C-TEP-IRM
summary: Main objective: The primary objective of the NA2C-PET-MRI study is to evaluate in vivo, using the radiotracer [¹¹C]ORM-13070, the effect of normal aging and Parkinson's disease on the availability of α₂C-adrenergic receptors in the human brain.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Healthy volunteers : Age between 20 years and 80 years
2. Patients : Weight between 40kg and 100kg
3. Patients : With an idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (Dopa-sensitive)
4. Patients : Without head trauma history including loss of consciousness superior to 30 minutes
5. Patients : Without associated neurological pathology
6. Patients : With highly effective contraception for women of childbearing age
7. Patients : Affiliated to a social security or similar scheme
8. Patients : Not subject to any legal protection measures
9. Patients : Participant must have signed an informed consent document
10. Healthy volunteers : Weight between 40kg and 100kg
11. Healthy volunteers : Without neurologic or psychiatric history
12. Healthy volunteers : Without head trauma history including loss of consciousness superior to 30 minutes
13. Healthy volunteers : With highly effective contraception for women of childbearing age
14. Healthy volunteers : Affiliated to a social security or similar scheme
15. Healthy volunteers : Not subject to any legal protection measures
16. Healthy volunteers : Participant must have signed an informed consent document
17. Patients : Age between 40 years and 80 years
Exclusion criteria:
1. Subject receiving (or having received in the last month) somatic medication with cerebral or psychological effects (e.g., antihistamines)
2. Persons receiving psychiatric care
3. Persons admitted to a health or social care facility for purposes other than research
4. Subjects with a current or past dependence on alcohol or any other addictive substance according to DSM-IV-TR criteria, with the exception of nicotine and caffeine
5. Subjects already participating in another biomedical research project or who have participated in a study using ionizing radiation within the past year
6. Pregnant woman parturient or breastfeeding
7. MRI contraindications : people using pacemaker or insulin pumps, with implanted or embedded metal objects in the head or body, claustrophobic, with neurosensory stimulators or implantable defibrillators, with cochlear implants, with ferromagnetic foreign bodies in the eye or brain close to nerve structures, agitation of the subject (uncooperative or agitated subjects), ventriculoperitoneal neurosurgical shunt valves, dental appliances
8. Subject with a contraindication to PET scans at the ORM : hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients (sodium chloride)
9. Subjects who are unable to understand or complete the study (language barrier, obvious lack of motivation, etc.) as judged by the investigator
10. Subjects who do not agree to be informed in the event of an incidental finding of an abnormality on MRI or during neuropsychological assessment
11. Persons deprived of their liberty by judicial or administrative decision
